title: Dispatch: Accept a later-revoked successor in the campaign-rule set validator (PR #524 review 6, head 671c9a9)
description:
External review #5119130556 (2026-09-05) of PR #524 head 671c9a9: CHANGES REQUIRED, ONE blocking finding. Review-5 revocation-history blocker CONFIRMED FIXED (rev11-13). Supervisor REPRODUCED the new one at 671c9a9.

WORKTREE / BRANCH: .worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev14 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev14, cut from eshyra-jhpt at 671c9a9. npm ci already run.

FINDING (BLOCKING) — the .1 set validator rejects a canonical lifecycle that .2 intentionally creates.
campaignRules.ts::validateCampaignRules resolves rule.supersededBy and unconditionally fails with 'a revoked rule cannot supersede another rule' when successor.status === 'revoked'. But a successor that validly superseded its prior and was LATER revoked is a legitimate history: .5 explicitly allows edit-by-supersession then revocation, and the reviewer-required R5 test creates exactly r5-original -> r5-successor then revokes r5-successor. SUPERVISOR REPRO at 671c9a9: create A (effective 1, current 0); persist turn 1; supersede A with B (effective 2); revoke B at ordinal 3; listCampaignRules returns [A superseded, B revoked]; validateCampaignRules(rules) throws 'CampaignRuleError: a revoked rule cannot supersede another rule'. The transition-time invariant is ALREADY enforced at the right boundary: supersedeCampaignRule rejects a prior whose CURRENT status is not active, and the successor is written through the live create path as active. The set-level check wrongly treats a LATER status as proof about the EARLIER transition. The existing domain test (campaignRules.test.ts ~line 295) builds a revoked successor with revokedPosition null and asserts only .toThrow('revoked'), so the single-record 'revoked rule must carry revokedPosition' guard fires first and the set-level check is never actually exercised — a false green.

REQUIRED FIX (supervisor decision):
1. In validateCampaignRules, REMOVE the `successor.status === 'revoked'` rejection. Keep: successor existence, cross-campaign rejection, cycle detection, per-rule validation, duplicate identity. Do not add any replacement status-based assumption about the successor (a superseded successor is also valid history: A -> B -> C).
2. Keep supersedeCampaignRule's live guards exactly as they are ('campaign rule X is revoked' / 'is already superseded' for a non-active prior).
3. Repair campaignRules.test.ts: the revoked-successor case must build a COHERENT revoked successor (revokedPosition set) and now assert that validateCampaignRules ACCEPTS the graph {A supersededBy B, B revoked with revokedPosition}; also assert a longer chain A->B->C with C revoked is accepted. Remove the broad .toThrow('revoked') false green. Keep a separate test proving the single-record guard 'revoked rule must carry revokedPosition' still rejects an incoherent revoked rule.

PERMANENT EVIDENCE (each must FAIL against 671c9a9):
V1 (store test, real .2 APIs): create A, supersede A with B, revoke B, then validateCampaignRules(listCampaignRules(db, { campaignId })) does not throw; the returned pair matches [A superseded/supersededBy B, B revoked with the canonical revokedPosition].
V2 (store test): superseding an already-revoked PRIOR through supersedeCampaignRule is rejected with the exact message "campaign rule 'X' is revoked" and leaves the prior unchanged (may extend the existing 'rejects superseding a revoked rule' test — confirm it asserts the exact message).
V3 (domain test): the coherent graph above is accepted directly by validateCampaignRules.
NEGATIVE PROOF: run the new/changed tests against 671c9a9 before fixing; report observed counts and quote messages. Do NOT change anything else (no store, migration, position, admission, or context changes).

VERIFICATION: npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing; report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local resolution.
